dedupe_keys.name: a multi modal multi temporal multi resolution benchmark dataset for building height estimation

description: A Multi-Modal, Multi-Temporal, Multi-Resolution Benchmark Dataset for Building Height Estimation is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Ritu Yadav et al. Building heights are used in sustainable urban planning and monitoring. While traditional methods use airborne stereo images and LiDAR data for accurate height estimation, their large-scale application is costly and slow, limiting the ability to conduct frequent large-scale monitoring. In contrast, satellite data offers a scalable alternative, further improved with Deep Learning (DL) models. Coverage: a single site or case study; published in 2025. Formats: GeoTIFF, Image. The data are held in Hugging Face and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support building-stock, asset and facility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
